text: Behavioral Warning (The Isolation Trap): This protocol demands starving your brain of "Phasic" Dopamine (excitement, novelty, the chase), and the easiest way to do that is to hole up alone. But do not isolate completely, because total social isolation spikes cortisol, the chronic stress hormone, and that sensitizes your brain to glutamate and locks the armor in place even if you've never had an addiction. You still need the "Oxytocinergic Anchoring" of having people around you, as long as it's the calm kind of company.
section: A Complete Guide to Bio-De-Armoring, the warnings at the top: the Behavioral Warning
reader: an adult with trauma or an addiction who has read the short introduction and is reading the warnings before starting the protocol, who tends to withdraw from people when working on themselves

marked.s: Behavioral Warning (The Isolation Trap): This protocol demands starving your brain of "Phasic" Dopamine (excitement, novelty, the chase), and the easiest way to do that is to hole up alone, but do not isolate completely.
Total social isolation spikes cortisol, the chronic stress hormone, which makes your brain more sensitive to glutamate, and that locks the armor in place whether or not you've ever had an addiction.
We're social animals, so you still need people, just the calm kind, whose company gives you oxytocin instead of a dopamine spike (the "Oxytocinergic Anchoring" the rule below is about).
